title: ABC-FHE: A Resource-Efficient Accelerator Enabling Bootstrappable Parameters for Client-Side Fully Homomorphic Encryption
problem: Client-side Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) computations remain a bottleneck, particularly under bootstrappable parameter configurations involving encoding, encryption, decoding, and decryption for large parameters, requiring 10,000-fold more computation than plaintext processing.
motivation: While server-side FHE acceleration has advanced, privacy-preserving applications require efficient client-side processing which is hindered by polynomial computational overhead and memory requirements.
method: ABC-FHE employs a streaming architecture with a reconfigurable Fourier engine capable of switching between NTT (Number-Theoretic Transform) and FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) modes. It includes an on-chip pseudo-random number generator and unified on-the-fly twiddle factor generator to reduce memory demands, with optimized task scheduling to enhance CKKS client-side processing, reducing off-chip memory access.
key_novelty: Reconfigurable dual-mode Fourier engine (NTT/FFT) with on-chip PRNG and unified twiddle generation to eliminate bottlenecks in bootstrappable FHE parameter processing while minimizing area.
contributions: Streaming architecture for high performance density and minimal area/off-chip memory access
Reconfigurable Fourier engine supporting both NTT and FFT modes for CKKS encoding/decryption
On-chip pseudo-random number generator and unified on-the-fly twiddle factor generation
1112x encoding/encryption speedup vs CPU, 214x vs SOTA client-side accelerator; 963x decoding/decryption speedup vs CPU, 82x vs SOTA

metrics.speedup: 1112x encoding/encryption vs CPU, 214x vs SOTA accelerator; 963x decoding/decryption vs CPU, 82x vs SOTA

limitations: Abstract does not discuss maximum number of levels of homomorphic operations, bootstrapping latency, or end-to-end application performance impact.
primary_theme: Reconfigurable ASIC for client-side FHE with dual Fourier engine
